## Context / Problem
5 local `make verify` runs of Nov 19-20 2026 ran inside the Claude Code agent sandbox (temp dirs under the sandbox TMPDIR `/private/tmp/claude-502`) and each failed 37 to 45 tests that pass in CI. The 5 complete unsandboxed runs failed none of these.

## Verified cause
A controlled A/B on Nov 20 2026 ran one fixed set of 21 test modules (origin/main 8e1d15e664f, `-n 4`, same host, minutes apart, load 17-21). Outside the sandbox all 379 tests passed in 187.58 s. Inside, 18 failed and 3 errored (655.42 s). Every failure traces to 2 capabilities the sandbox denies, each reproduced directly in a sandboxed shell:
- AF_UNIX sockets. `socket(AF_UNIX).bind()` in the temp dir raises `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`. Breaks all 9 tests in `tests/unit/test_reclaim_resign.py` (their private `ssh-agent -a <sock>` never binds, so `ssh-add` fails) and both tests in `tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py`.
- Outbound HTTPS to 2 hosts:
  - `semgrep.dev`. The opengrep/semgrep backend pre-validates each detector with `semgrep --validate`, which downloads the `p/semgrep-rule-lints` ruleset from `semgrep.dev`. In the sandbox that request is denied (`deny network-outbound semgrep.dev:443`), so validation retries for about 60 s and the harness abstains. This fails 4 tests in `tests/unit/test_code_review_conflict_markers.py` / `test_code_review_public_exposure.py` (their negative tests pass falsely after 122 s each) and 2 in `tests/unit/grounding/test_conformance.py`. The existing `configure_semgrep_settings_file` redirect (ticket 985f-0ec5) works: with it `semgrep scan` succeeds in the sandbox; only `--validate` fails, on the network.
  - `pypi.org`. Isolated builds (`python -m build`) cannot fetch `hatchling` (`deny network-outbound pypi.org:443`): the 3 `tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py` errors and `tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py::test_hook_falls_back_to_git_when_env_unset`.
These are not test defects: CI hosts provide both capabilities, and a per-test shim cannot cover them because the denied capability is the operation under test.

## Approach
`make verify` refuses up front on a host that lacks one of these capabilities, and says which, instead of a misleading red (or false green) after 25 minutes.
- New `scripts/check_verify_host.py` (marked `# mechanism-ok: ci_gate scripts/check_verify_host.py — d492-04db-b79e-428f`). Three probes, each a function returning `(ok, detail)` and taking its I/O as an injectable argument for tests:
  1. `unix_socket_probe(socket_factory=socket.socket)`: bind, listen and connect an AF_UNIX socket in a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp()` directory, then remove it.
  2. `package_index_probe(runner=subprocess.run)`: write a minimal throwaway project (`pyproject.toml` with `build-backend = "hatchling.build"`) to a temp dir and run `[sys.executable, "-m", "build", "--outdir", <tmp>, <project>]` with `timeout=300` and the inherited environment. That is the command `tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py` runs (sdist, then a wheel from it), with the same isolated-env install of `hatchling` from the package index and the same pip cache, so the probe and the tests see the same network and cache state.
  3. `semgrep_validate_probe(runner=subprocess.run, which=shutil.which)`: when neither `opengrep` nor `semgrep` is on PATH it passes (those tests skip without an engine); otherwise it runs `<engine> --validate --config <one-rule temp file> --metrics=off` (the same flags `_opengrep_validate` in `src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py` passes) with `timeout=300`. It points `SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE` and `SEMGREP_LOG_FILE` into its temp dir, mirroring the test session's own redirect (`configure_semgrep_settings_file`, called from `tests/conftest.py`, which uses `.rebar/scratch/pytest-sandbox-<pid>/`), so a host whose home directory is unwritable is not refused for a cause the suite already handles; the probe then fails only on what the tests would fail on, the rule-lint download.
  Each failed probe prints one line naming the capability and the error detail (no test lists, so the message cannot go stale), followed by one closing line: `make verify` needs these to give the same verdict as CI; run it where they are available (for an agent sandbox, outside it), see docs/local-dev-env.md. Exit 1 on any failure, 0 and no output otherwise. A probe that raises unexpectedly is reported as that capability failing, with the exception text. The probes are not retried: a transient network failure costs a re-run of a 10-second preflight, not of a 25-minute suite. The script imports nothing from `tests/`, so it does not reuse `tests/_sandbox_capabilities.CapabilityProbe`.
- `Makefile`: new `verify-host` target running the script. `verify` becomes `verify: verify-host` with the recipe `@$(MAKE) --no-print-directory lint typecheck import-convention test`, so the preflight strictly precedes the gates even under `make -j` or `-k` (a failed prerequisite means the recipe never starts), while the sub-make keeps today's parallelism for the rest. The `##` help text on the `verify` line gains "host-capability preflight". `make test` and its two pytest lines stay unchanged, so `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` is unaffected. No skip is added anywhere.
- Docs: in `docs/local-dev-env.md`, a "Where `make verify` can run" subsection naming the 2 capabilities and the agent-sandbox case; correct the "Sandboxed agent hosts without POSIX named semaphores" subsection, whose claim that the counted-skip probes "restore a real `make verify` verdict under the sandbox" is no longer true (the shims stay for targeted pytest runs); update the `make verify` line in the command list (line ~547) and the "stops at the failing prerequisite" paragraph to include the preflight. In `AGENTS.md`, add `verify-host` to the `make verify` formula and one sentence pointing to the new subsection.
- No config key, environment variable, or command-line flag is added.

## Scope
- `scripts/check_verify_host.py` (new)
- `tests/unit/test_check_verify_host.py` (new)
- `Makefile`
- `docs/local-dev-env.md`
- `AGENTS.md`

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_check_verify_host.py`, all through the injected seams (no real network, no permission-bit tricks): each probe's pass path; AF_UNIX `PermissionError`; build runner returning exit 1 and raising `TimeoutExpired`; semgrep runner returning exit 2; no engine on PATH passes; `main()` with 2 failing probes prints both capability lines plus the closing line and exits 1; `main()` with all passing prints nothing and exits 0; a probe raising `RuntimeError` is reported as a failure, not a crash.
- A test parses the Makefile and asserts `verify`'s only prerequisite is `verify-host` and its recipe runs `lint typecheck import-convention test`.
- Manual, recorded on this ticket: inside the agent sandbox `make verify` exits 1 before `lint`, naming AF_UNIX sockets and network access; outside it `make verify-host` exits 0 silently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Inside the agent sandbox, `make verify` stops before `lint` with a message naming the denied capabilities (AF_UNIX sockets and outbound HTTPS to the package index and semgrep.dev), recorded on this ticket.
- [x] Outside the sandbox, `make verify-host` exits 0 with no output, and the full `make verify` passes on the change (run unsandboxed through the operator's host-local verify-slot wrapper, which only caps concurrent runs and then calls `make verify`), recorded on this ticket.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_check_verify_host.py` covers each probe's pass and fail path, the exception path, and the Makefile ordering.
- [x] `docs/local-dev-env.md` and `AGENTS.md` state where `make verify` can run, and no doc still says the sandbox shims restore a real `make verify` verdict.
- [x] Gerrit gives Verified +1. (3492 merged as 2693d59a047; evidence for every box is in the comments, including the cache-warm package-index pass inside the sandbox)
